clue.text: Drug mother knocked back direct

parts.note: an everyday word for mother

indicators.note: something knocked back is pushed the other way, so the word it follows is read from the end

parts.note: to direct a weapon is to aim it

explanation.surface: A mother has been dosed with a drug and has her directions all knocked out of her.
explanation.walkthrough: Mummia is an old word, kept in Chambers, for ground-up mummy flesh once sold as medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Powdered mummified remains were prescribed by apothecaries as a medicinal substance, hence a drug.

clue.text: Farming association from Missouri pretended to comprehend verse translation of Ovid (11, two words)

parts.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for Missouri

indicators.note: to comprehend is to include, so the pretence word wraps around what follows
a translation renders a text anew, so the poet's name is turned into a fresh order

parts.note: sham means pretended or fake
V is the abbreviation for verse
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A farming collective from Missouri claimed to understand a verse translation of the Roman poet Ovid.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAM opens after its third letter to take in V and the shuffled poet's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A moshav ovdim is an Israeli cooperative settlement of smallholders, an association of farmers.

clue.text: Tutor cut short Jamaican song and dance

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a mentor is an adviser or tutor

explanation.surface: A teacher stops a Caribbean musical performance before it ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Mento is a Jamaican folk music style, and the dance performed to it, a forerunner of ska.

clue.text: Infatuation, a muddle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a crush, as in the old slang to be ... on someone
second meaning: a soft mixed-up mass

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a comment on love, but the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives the noun as slang for a crush or infatuation, and also as a confused jumble or mess.

clue.text: Section from province deployed to follow royal procession? Rarely

indicators.note: a section is a slice cut out of a longer run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Troops are sent from a region to escort the monarch's procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' flags a rare word. 'Deployed' suggests troops, but it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To incede is a rare verb for walking in a stately way, as one would in a royal procession.

clue.text: HM has left fellow for stay in Scotland

indicators.note: the royal letters have departed, so they are taken out of the word that follows

parts.note: a sister is a fellow woman or comrade
Her Majesty is ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A report that Her Majesty has walked out on a companion, mentioning a stay north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ER from SISTER leaves SIST.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots law to sist is to stay or suspend legal proceedings, so the word is a Scottish term for stay.

clue.text: Small fish boiled the old way, with odd bits of corn in

indicators.note: with something in it, the outer word holds the chosen letters inside

parts.note: sod is an old past tense of seethe, to boil

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first and third, are the ones kept

parts.note: the first and third letters

explanation.surface: A recipe for a little fish, boiled in the traditional manner with a few kernels of corn.
explanation.walkthrough: Sod, the old past tense of seethe, is the boiled 'the old way'; seethe once meant simply to boil.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrod is the American term for a young cod or haddock, a small fish.

clue.text: Georgian once favoured, seen round former Russian strong man

indicators.note: something round another surrounds it, so the favoured word wraps the strongman

parts.note: in favour, popular
Lavrenti Beria was Stalin's feared secret police chief

explanation.surface: A man from Georgia, once in favour, is seen near a former Soviet strongman.
explanation.walkthrough: Beria was himself Georgian, which makes the surface apt. Iberia was the classical name for the land in the Caucasus.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberia was the ancient name for eastern Georgia in the Caucasus, so an Iberian was a Georgian of old.

clue.text: Muscle relaxant, nuclear war's chemical agent

parts.note: Soma is a brand of carisoprodol, a muscle relaxant drug
N is the abbreviation for nuclear

explanation.surface: A list of weapons: a drug that relaxes muscles, nuclear warfare, a chemical agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuclear war' looks like one phrase, but the split falls between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Soman is a nerve gas developed for chemical warfare, a military chemical agent.

clue.text: In mixing with some lawyers use this term for cash

definitions.text: lawyers use this term for cash

indicators.note: things being mixed are stirred together, so these letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note on legal jargon: when mingling with certain lawyers, use their word for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Monies, the plural of money, is used in legal and financial documents to mean sums of cash.

clue.text: Deluxe model: with new interior cost's special

indicators.note: having something as its interior means it is placed inside the next word

parts.note: cost is price, with the possessive s
N is the abbreviation for new
S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: A sales pitch for a top-of-the-range car with a refitted interior at a special price.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes into PRICE'S after its third letter, then S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess is used as a name for top-range products, such as the Austin Princess, implying a luxury version.

clue.text: Halts a beery drunk — to test thus?

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so these letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: the eleven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A police officer stops a driver who has been drinking beer, to check them in the usual way.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole scene: a beery driver who has been halted is the one tested this way.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathalyse is to test a driver's breath for alcohol, which is how a beery motorist is checked.

clue.text: What can describe voyage that's over — can ice drifting?

indicators.note: drifting things move about aimlessly, so these letters wander out of order

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for over
the six letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about whether a sea voyage is finished, now that tins of ice are floating about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' reads as finished, but it is just the cricket abbreviation O.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean crossing is an oceanic voyage, so the adjective is one way of describing such a trip.

clue.text: What measures lowness of pressure — or height?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a unit used for very low pressures, as in vacuums
second meaning: a variant spelling of tor, a rocky hill

explanation.walkthrough: Chambers gives torr as a spelling of tor, a hill or rocky peak, as on Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: The torr, named after Torricelli, is a small unit of pressure; a tor or torr is a hilltop, a height.

clue.text: ER comes dancing in a Scottish plimsoll, i.e. informally (13, two words)

indicators.note: one lot of letters goes inside the shoe word that follows
dancers move about, so these letters step out of their order

parts.note: the seven letters rearranged
a sannie is Scots for a sandshoe or plimsoll

explanation.surface: The Queen arrives at a dance wearing a Scottish gym shoe, the very picture of informality.
explanation.walkthrough: A plimsoll is a light canvas sports shoe; sannie is short for sandshoe in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means without ceremony, which is a borrowed way of saying casually or informally.

clue.text: Wild fancy about embracing unnamed male goes on a long time?

indicators.note: the time word continues after what comes first, added at the end
an embrace wraps around something, so the about word encloses the next

parts.note: ca, circa, means about
the pronoun stands for a man without naming him
an era is a long period

explanation.surface: A daydream about holding a man who is not named runs on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimaera is a fanciful, unrealistic idea, named after the monster of Greek myth, so a wild fancy.

clue.text: Small openings for an Asiatic bird

parts.note: taken as written
the indefinite article
the mina or myna is an Asian starling

explanation.surface: Little holes made for an Asian bird, perhaps in a nesting box.
explanation.definitionFit: Foramina is the plural of foramen, the anatomical term for a small hole or aperture.

clue.text: Well, well! Ancient getting to grips

parts.note: an exclamation of surprise
a synonym

explanation.surface: Someone remarks with surprise that an old person is finally coming to terms with something.
explanation.walkthrough: Get ahold of is the North American idiom for grasp, so ahold stands for to grips after getting.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting ahold and getting to grips both mean taking a firm grasp, so the adverb replaces the phrase.

clue.text: Form of rat, I, corrupt, switching sides?

definitions.note: a phrase describing the person, standing for the noun

indicators.note: a new form is a reshaping, so the letters are recast in another order

parts.note: taken as written
to rot is to corrupt or decay

explanation.surface: A confession that one is a rat, crooked and turning coat.
explanation.walkthrough: A rat is also slang for a traitor, which makes 'Form of rat' apt in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor betrays his own side, effectively changing allegiance to the enemy.

clue.text: Bug head of church secreted in mitre?

indicators.note: something secreted is hidden away inside, so the letter goes within the next word

parts.note: in sewing a mitre is a triangular piece let into a garment, an inset

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of church

explanation.surface: A tiny creature has been hidden inside a bishop's tall hat by the senior churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop's mitre is the red herring; the needlework mitre, a triangular insert, is the piece meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Bug is the informal word for an insect, so the two are interchangeable.

clue.text: To make sovereign smile I played round EP air, funny

indicators.note: letters that are played with are moved about into a new order
something funny is odd or strange, so these letters come out jumbled
the first group of letters goes around the second

parts.note: the six letters rearranged
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone smiles while playing a comic tune from an old extended-play record.
explanation.walkthrough: An EP is an extended-play record. Two anagram signals work on two separate groups, one wrapped round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperialise is to give imperial status or rule, that is to make something sovereign.

clue.text: Stone lifted on edge, revealing sort of sole

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting something turns it upward, so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone
a rim is an edge; on places it after

explanation.surface: A rock is raised on its edge, exposing a flatfish hidden underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: The megrim is a European flatfish, also called the sail-fluke, related to the soles.

clue.text: Tropical bean, little length, one to give away

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for length
a means one
to blab is to give away a secret

explanation.surface: A seed merchant offers a small amount of tropical bean, one to give away free.
explanation.definitionFit: Lablab is the hyacinth bean, a climbing legume grown in tropical regions for food.

clue.text: An involuntary agitation almost reverses code of silence

indicators.note: the words before it are turned round and read backwards
almost means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the indefinite article
a tremor is an involuntary shaking

explanation.surface: A nervous shudder nearly overturns a vow of silence.
explanation.walkthrough: TREMOR loses its last letter, then A and TREMO are read backwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: Omertà is the Mafia's rule of keeping silent before the authorities, a code of silence.

clue.text: Forgotten the words? Use this bit of neutral articulation

indicators.note: a bit is a small piece cut out of a longer run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Advice for a singer who has forgotten the lyrics: sing a meaningless sound instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole question; 'neutral articulation' also describes the sound itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Tra-la is a nonsense refrain sung in place of lyrics, just what one sings when the words have gone.

clue.text: Make tracks as energy-filled entertainment (5, two words)

indicators.note: something filled has contents put inside it, so the energy letter goes in

parts.note: a boff is slang for a hit show or a big laugh
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Head off to a lively show full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make tracks' is the informal phrase for leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Be off is an instruction to leave, the same as to make tracks or depart.

clue.text: One named for a rock star's No. 1 getting into trouble with one

indicators.note: one letter enters after the trouble word and before the one word, joining them

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

indicators.note: the number one position is the first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of star
a means one

explanation.surface: A rock star whose top hit landed them in trouble alongside someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: Ailsa Craig is a rocky island in the Firth of Clyde, and the girl's name comes from it. The 'rock star' surface misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailsa is a girl's name taken from the island of Ailsa Craig, so its bearer is named after a rock.

clue.text: Slow movement, last (second) omitted from Renaissance composer

indicators.note: whatever is omitted is left out of the following name

parts.note: Orlande de Lassus, the Franco-Flemish composer
the last one, and S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: The final slow section by a Renaissance composer has been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: LASSUS loses its final S, the last letter that is an S for second.
explanation.definitionFit: The lassu is the slow opening section of the csárdás, the Hungarian dance, so it is a slow movement.

clue.text: Deviates when taking in Georgia ramblings

indicators.note: to take in is to receive inside, so the state goes within the first word

parts.note: to vary is to deviate
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A traveller strays from the route while wandering through the American state of Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deviates' looks like the definition, a verb, but it is the outer wordplay; the definition is the noun at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Vagaries are whims or wanderings of the mind, from Latin vagari, to wander, hence ramblings.

clue.text: Deportment I intrinsically follow being brought up

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing something up turns it to read from the bottom
intrinsically means within itself, so the letter goes inside the following word

parts.note: to tag along is to follow
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone says their manners come naturally from how they were raised.
explanation.walkthrough: TAG takes in I to make TIAG, which is then read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Gait is the manner of walking or carrying oneself, a sense of bearing close to deportment.

clue.text: Year after a palm's rotted badly — grafting required?

indicators.note: something rotted badly has fallen apart, so these letters lose their order
coming after means placed later, so the year letter is sent to the end

parts.note: the letters of a palm's and rotted rearranged
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A year after a palm tree has rotted, the gardener asks whether grafting is needed to save it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotted' does double duty as fodder and part of the indicator 'rotted badly'. Grafting suggests horticulture, but the skin kind is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Dermatoplasty is plastic surgery of the skin, typically by skin grafting, so it is what is needed when a graft is called for.

clue.text: Member of plant family from Ireland I had clipped

indicators.note: a clipped phrase is cut short, with letters snipped out of the contraction

parts.note: IR is an abbreviation for Ireland
shortened to I'd

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a plant they once grew back in Ireland, before it was cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: An irid is any plant of the iris family, Iridaceae, so it belongs to that plant family.

clue.text: Head of fortifications erects palisades

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of fortifications
to raise is to erect

explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' reads as a person in charge but only picks out a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraise is a defensive fence of pointed stakes set horizontally on a rampart, a type of palisade.

clue.text: Throw up noisily at rear of saloon

indicators.note: the loud letter is placed after the saloon word, at its back end

parts.note: a saloon is a bar

explanation.walkthrough: 'Noisily' looks like part of the definition; it is the musical forte, F.

clue.text: Misshapen bust secured by bits of old elastic, not pointed

indicators.note: the outer letters hold the shuffled word fast between them
something misshapen is bent out of form, so these letters are rearranged
only small parts, here the opening letters, of the next words are used

parts.note: the first letter of old
the four letters rearranged
the first letter of elastic

explanation.surface: An ill-fitting bra held up with scraps of old elastic, a rather blunt garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means blunt or rounded at the tip, the opposite of sharp, so not pointed.
